verdict.tagline: Space exploration laced with brutal losses and unforgettable triumphs.
for_you_if: you love deep strategic space rogue-likes
you enjoy overcoming punishing difficulty spikes
you appreciate extensive community modding support
not_for_you_if: you hate losing runs to sudden random chance
you struggle with steep learning curves
you prefer guaranteed progress over trial and error

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as very steep and note that the game has an unforgiving difficulty curve.

citations.review_text:
If I had several hours every day to play video games, I would get so into FTL. And over months and years, I may still get very into it.
But I've never played an indie game that makes me feel like League of Legends or Hearthstone or other big title matchmaking games do, and FTL does.
The learning curve is very steep. Playing easy feels like most of my runs succeed or at least get to the end.
Yet somehow, playing medium feels like one out of dozens of runs gets to the end.
I hate the rng variance. Without looking up advice or probabilities from experienced players, I have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue how to track how often I will get absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by a distress beacon or other random event.
Sometimes I get 40 scrap or an upgrade randomly, then sometimes I lose a crewmember. Maybe players with 100+ hours know why, I sure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ don't.
If I had hours and hours to play this game, and maybe one day I will put hours and hours in, I could learn it well enough to have consistent runs.
At the moment, I love the design and concept, but most of my medium runs just get stomped by rng variance. The game is fun until its not, and then I wonder why I've wasted 2-3 hours and now I feel far worse than I did when I started playing, and I have to work tomorrow, and I feel unsatisfied and like I've wasted my time. That's how League of Legends and other big title games feel. That's how FTL feels to me right now. ♥♥♥♥ this stupid ass beautiful game. I wish the devs had just added another difficulty in between easy and medium, or decreased the rng variance in events or the amount of events because its so hard to track what is going to happen.
AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
Really really hard for the first few runs and very unforgiving, but once you learn the basics it gets really fun and only a tad bit hard.
Enjoyable game, but be ready for an unforgiving difficulty curve into the mid-to-late parts of runs!

Just another horribly balanced indie game that sweaty weirdos will tell you that you have a "skill issue" at. It scales terribly even on easy, relies entirely on random chance and skill and tactics only take you so far. It's a short game that forces you to move quickly through each stage while getting upgrades along the way, if you're lucky enough to find them, punishes you for getting too many too quick or not enough too late and craps on you for going too far too soon, while not telling you in any way what you're doing wrong. 

I hate having my hand held in games, but this is like hand swatting whenever you try something. Wouldn't recommend to anyone that just wants typical fun in a game, that is simply fun. If you like being angry at pixels then this is probably for you.
It can feel really unbalanced if runs get ended over and over by bad luck, which then causes the game to feel repetitive. Apart from that its cool, maybe more rouge upgrades would be nice
I want to like the game, but i can't recomment it... For the amount of options avalible to you there is to much RNG.

For the price it is worth it.

The game is unbalanced and the RNG in this game will make you go insane, if the price was a bit higher it would've been a negative review.

I can say with confidence that you shouldn't buy this.

Like most other people who don't like the game, I think the rng completely ruins the experience. Don't listen to the people stating that there's individuals with win streaks of 90 or whatever, because immediately after telling you you're just bad they'll tell you to learn every single detail of any event and essentially memorize the wiki to actually enjoy the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it'll throw at you.

If you want a good rougelike, play TBOI, Mewgenics, Enter the Gungeon, or the Void War demo in particular if you want something similar without the unfair events and inconsistent difficulty.  The worst part about this game is that you only realize that you want a refund after you out more than a few hours in. 

Please read reviews, even negative ones. If I did, I wouldn't have wasted 10 dollars on this crap.

Honestly I don't feel like writing a whole review for this, so I'll keep it brief. I get the developers wanted to remove save scumming, but sometimes it'd down to complete RNG if you get put in a practically unwinnable situation. I'd end up spending 20 or so minutes getting almost to the end, just to have 5 intruders teleport to my ship and then blow up my medical and oxygen rooms. If you hate RNG dependent games, I don't think you'll find this very enjoyable. Maybe you will, who knows. But TLDR, you have to get very lucky to have an okay run. If you get unlucky, you have to restart the entire thing.

Not recommended.

Dark Souls, But in space. 

9/10 game, im not a fan of RNG making me lose, since how can a player learn if i die because i get unlucky, but aside from that fantastic game. making it diffcult is flat out genius, since it makes it one of the most replayable games for me.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features a pixel-art visual style accompanied by a soundtrack composed by Ben Prunty.

citations.review_text: Best pixel-art ship-to-ship combat roguelike that can (allegedly) run on the slowest of setups. Lot of different ship types to specialize in stealth, systems disruptions, boarding parties, mind control, or just blasting them out of the sky

Somehow, I've not already written a review for FTL? Wow, okay, here goes then.

FTL is a timeless masterpiece, and a roguelite so distinct that it has become the foundation of its own subgenre. I spent untold hundreds of hours playing FTL for over a decade to 100% completion (on the iPad version, so my depicted Steam playtime is quite misleading), and to this day it has aged like fine wine.

The gameplay systems are a masterclass in being easy to understand, but brutally hard to master. The pixel artstyle is crisp, Ben Prunty's soundtrack is wonderful, and there is a massive amount of replayability unlocking every ship and achievement. In terms of performance and graphical options, FTL is incredibly optimized, if now slightly dated. It is not designed for particularly high resolutions, but what do you expect from a game that's now almost 15 years old.

Eventually, you can get into modding as well if you still crave more content. The biggest total conversion mod, Multiverse, might as well be FTL 2 with how absurdly expansive it is. 

A common complaint about FTL that I have seen over the years is that it feels very RNG dependent, but as you reach higher level play, you begin to see that metagame strategy revolves around skill-based RNG mitigation, through proactive choices in ship-building and decision making. If this is still a dealbreaker for you, Subset Games' other main title, Into the Breach, is the perfect foil to FTL if you prefer strategy designed around absolute certainty instead.

Overall, FTL is one of my top 10 favourite games of all time, and a fundamental hallmark game that every strategy/roguelite fan owes it to themselves to play.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the final boss fight against the flagship differs significantly from standard encounters and catches players off guard without prior knowledge or guides.

citations.review_text: Hack stopped working during flagship battle and I couldn't breach their shields, first ever flagship fight on easy. 10/10 would recommend to casual players

It's the spaceship simulator. The classic. For the price I think everyone with a steam library should play this at least once. I enjoy it

Downsides - Your whole run is built around the Flagship, a cheating bastard that doesn't play like any of the other ships in the entire game. You don't know you're fighting the flagship until you get there, and it's incredibly frustrating until you find guides on what you're even doing.
Personally, I hate the flagship and think it's the worst part of this game. I recommend downloading one of those completed save files so you don't have to suffer the task of unlocking ships the "right" way.

Other than my burning, seething, odious hatred for the Flagship, this is easily one of my favorite sim games. It's peak

claims.claim: Reviewers report that runs feature text-based events with choices that can lead to unexpected consequences or crew member deaths.

citations.review_text:
I like that the game is really challenging.
The only thing that I don't like that you rarely know what you choose when you have options in events (that there is not that many types), and that ships are openned mostly through wining by previous type of ship, rather then finishing a quests.

Crew management, random encounters, rare events, an encroaching doom, danger and death at every turn. (keep away from the spiders!) 
One of my favorite games! Space Roguelike at its finest! 
Ultimate in replay ability.

Steepest learning curve, manually controlling every minute detail, crew AI functionally useless as the ship literally burns down around them, never receiving a weapon, or ammo for your weapons, just to run out of fuel or be killed by some RNG event... Honestly, I'm not sure where the enjoyment is here. Even on Easy mode a random event will just END your run out of nowhere.

EDIT: 

Ok... So, writing a review with new baby sleep deprivation will make you grumpy. I'm updating it now with new experiences. 

For one, the game gets better once you halfway understand what you're doing. Of course, that takes some research because the game really throws you into the deep end. Even the tutorial only prepares you so much. 

Even once you have an idea of what you're doing, though, the game is HARD. I played on easy for many hours and eventually won a few runs, and I'd say I got the hang of the game. I ended up setting it back to normal mode and it was BRUTAL. So I guess I still have a lot to learn. Fine. That being said, there really are some random "feels bad" occurrences. Send a crew member to check it out? Oh now they're dead... ok cool so I guess I'll just lose? This game is known for being punishing like that. When the RNG falls in your favor, it rarely feels like enough to balance things out. Sometimes the game just takes a cheap shot and you get hosed. 

I want to start playing on Normal mode, but man, the difficulty REALLY ramps up, and it feels like the way the game does this is by hitting you with random bad luck. Get boarded? Cool. Your ship is on fire and your crew are dying and even if you manage to micromanage your crew out of the bad situation, you're still going to get hit by that random missile and die. It... feels bad. 

That being said - I like the game. I've changed the review to Recommend. I don't actually have the number of hours shown here because too often the game gets paused and I walk away from it to take care of new baby, or tend to wife, or whateve…

Incredible game. Do yourself a favor and get the Multiverse mod after you've beaten FTL unmodded. Multiverse is basically everything you would want FTL 2 to be, and it is free.

10/10 Roguelike. Vanilla is fantastic on it's own. FTL: Multiverse is even better. 

Ships shooting it out in the vacuum of space. Variable encounters with multiple outcomes. Each ship has it's strength and weakness. Some fight with weapons, and others with crew/drones. Entertaining worldbuilding without too much depth, providing a open (though established) set of playable races & lore.
Each run might end the same (in vanilla), but the way you approach it can vary in ways you may not expect!

If you like hard games, a bit of random chance, and solid re-playable title - this is the game for you. 

HIGHLY RECOMMEND: Multiverse Mod + Hyperspace

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as exceptionally difficult, requiring dozens of hours before achieving a first win even on the easiest difficulty setting.

citations.review_text: I'd love to give this game a bad review, but that doesn't feel right. I've played for 35 hours and haven't even won on the easiest difficulty level. It's very frustrating.

This game is so stupidly hard. So so so hard. Ridiculously hard. Hardest game I've ever played. This is harder than Eldin Ring. I just now had the perfect run and then decided to attack an auto scout and I died. I hate this game so much but I love it so much. It's addicting. Almost 40 hours in and I still haven't even come close to beating easy mode. This is painful. Honestly just awful. This game keeps me up at night. It's so mind-numbingly difficult that I haven't been thinking straight.
10/10, would recommend.

Be prepared to lose hours of your life and your mind trying to beat this game even once.

Update: I finally managed to beat the BASE mode on EASY after just over 50 hours.
